Planner note: the comment is right. The inspection gate in skills_registry.transition() must apply to EVERY transition whose target state is "testing" for a record that is not provenance builtin (discovered → testing, disabled → testing, quarantined → testing), not only to quarantined → testing: refuse without findings.json ("not inspected"), refuse on max_severity block unless the reason starts with the override prefix, record overrides in history. Add tests/test_skill_discovery.py::test_every_path_into_testing_requires_inspection (discovered → testing and disabled → testing both refused for an uninspected external record; builtin records unaffected).
acceptance: docs/skill-intelligence/07-external.md exists; `uv run orchestrator skills discover skills` (local path) runs and refuses builtins; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

result.summary: The gate in _testing_findings now triggers whenever record["provenance"] != "builtin" (in addition to old_state=="quarantined"), so every non-builtin entry into testing is covered: discovered->testing, disabled->testing, demoted->testing, shadow->testing, and quarantined->testing, plus rollback-into-testing. Verified provenance for external skills is always "repository" or "external", never "builtin", so builtins are unaffected. Ran tests/test_skill_discovery.py directly (13 tests, including the new test_every_path_into_testing_requires_inspection which iterates every ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS origin into testing plus the rollback path) — all pass. This closes the exact loophole the rejected review comment identified.

comments.issue: rollback() calls _testing_findings to gate re-entry into testing but discards the returned finding_ids instead of recording them on the rollback history entry (transition() does record them via override/finding_ids). Not a bypass and no acceptance criterion covers it, just an inconsistency with the transition() path.
